ratings_why.fun: The lead queue, the Banner walking down the line and Kits as timers make each fight a story, but most bought Lemmings sit silent and Tiers 1-3 compete for one End of Turn slot, so the early board feels flat.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because one printed rule (only your Front speaks) turns reading order into a queue of speakers where death hands off the lead; no tribe today gates every card's text on position like this.

verdict_why: Old Mother Lemen, the Matriarch build's centre, still doesn't say whether damage to her shrinks every Kit; that one fix is worth a pass.

points.text: Old Mother Lemen: "current Attack and Health" doesn't say whether damage she takes lowers every Kit's Health mid-fight, or whether a hit Kit loses its own copy. Say "her Attack and full Health" or state that damage is tracked per Kit.
The fantasy lands in what the cards do: Pilgrims dying to raise the Banner, Gerd drawing every hit, Council meeting on the move. Keep it; it reads as lemmings, not as a generic token tribe.
Tiers 1-3 are almost all silent unless in front. One Loud Tier 1 or 2 Lemming (say a squeaky Kit-maker) would make the early shop feel alive and teach the rule by contrast, as Tally does.

The Front Lemming is the hardest card to read: doubled triggers, deferred swaps, then its own swap. Splitting it into "Take the Lead: your Take the Lead effects trigger twice this fight" plus a separate swap line would read faster.
Ole the Learned as Front fills slots ahead of itself, so its own Kit steals the lead. Filling only slots behind your Front keeps the raining-Kits joke without the beginner trap.

standouts.why: Gerd the Shouter reads in one glance and is the seed's shouter: he makes enemies hit whoever leads, which turns the death order into something you set.
Next-Cliff Pilgrim is the cliff cult in one line: it dies in front so the herd goes further.
Herding Council bends the one rule in a single sentence, and Loud makes it readable from any slot.

weakest.why: The Front Lemming's swap timing takes several reads, and it multiplies the tribe's most confusing part.
Kit-Minder fights Banner-Bearer, Herding Elder and Thaw Nester for the one End of Turn spot and gives the least.
Ole the Learned easily hands the lead to a blank Kit, so it reads as a trap more than a tool.

flags.note: Whether damage to Old Mother Lemen changes every Kit's Health mid-fight isn't stated.
Cantor of the Edge, then The Front Lemming, then golden Brother Onward can push the Banner past 15 and hand it to everyone twice.
Golden Herald of the Herd before Herding Elder or Banner-Bearer stacks End of Turn growth three times; fine as a high roll, worth watching.
